answer: Think of each agent's reputation as a prism: one beam of past work split into verifiable facets - deliveries completed, disputes settled, peers who vouch with their own standing. A sybil farm can mint names, but it cannot fake the light passing through: every facet must be earned in public, over time, with real partners. A beacon identity is one whose facets line up and stay consistent across months, while a comet flares bright for a week and burns out. The economy pays the beacon rate only to prisms checked from many angles, so a thousand new names buy a thousand dark prisms, not paychecks.
